title: Hybrid per-token rate model + uptime-crediting experiment for Hosted API
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run a controlled experiment that combines a hybrid input/output per-token pricing model with an uptime-crediting mechanism for customers who experience platform-level interruptions. Objective is to evaluate revenue impact, customer satisfaction, and friction to adoption for enterprise contracts that want stronger availability guarantees while preserving cost predictability for bursty streaming workloads.
motivation: Current per-token experiments focus on IO splits and streaming minimums independently. Enterprise customers request both more granular IO signaling (to align pricing with model compute characteristics) and contractual uptime credits for incidents. We need to quantify trade-offs and surface operational implications before baking into enterprise contract templates.
hypothesis: (1) Introducing a hybrid rate (lower output token price + slightly higher input token price) will improve perceived fairness for generative use cases and increase average revenue per customer by 4-8% for high-output workloads. (2) Offering an automatic uptime crediting policy (triggered by SLO breaches) will increase enterprise renewals by reducing churn risk for customers with strict availability needs.
experiment_design: A/B test with three cohorts over 8 weeks: control (current symmetric per-token pricing), hybrid-rate cohort (input price +X%, output price -Y%), and hybrid-rate-plus-credits cohort (same pricing plus automated uptime credits tied to monthly SLOs). Include both streaming and non-streaming routes. Minimum billing floors to be set at 100 API-seconds per month for streaming routes and a soft grace period of 72 hours after signup for credit eligibility.
metrics: Primary: net revenue per active customer (NRAC), monthly active customer churn, enterprise renewal intent (survey), customer satisfaction (NPS sub-question on pricing), and incidence of credit claims. Secondary: average tokens in/out ratio, streaming request latency percentiles (p50/p95), billing disputes opened.
success_criteria: Revenue uplift >= 3% with no more than 10% increase in billing disputes and neutral-to-positive enterprise renewal intent signal. If uptime-credit cohort yields >5% lower churn in customers with PII/reg compliance sensitivity, consider productizing.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal sandbox run with Canary customers (5 large enterprise customers coordinated via AE) for 2 weeks. 2) Open A/B pool to 10% of new signups and randomized 5% of existing customers who opt in (explicit consent required). 3) Monitor metrics daily and run interim analysis at week 4 and final analysis at week 8. 4) If success_criteria met, prepare PRD for enterprise contract language and Console UI toggles.
risks_mitigation:
- Customer confusion: add clear billing previews and examples in console and onboarding emails.
- Revenue downside if model mis-priced: cap exposure with a revenue guardrail that automatically reverts pricing for any customer segment losing >10% revenue over 7-day rolling window.
- Operational burden for credits: automate credit calculation and create dedicated dispute queue; pre-authorize finance owner for manual review during pilot.
- Security/compliance: ensure crediting logic does not leak customer usage data; security review required.
notes: We will coordinate with Sales to surface this experiment to select enterprise pilots; prepare FAQ and runbook for Support. Design needs to produce billing preview comps for both admin console and invoice PDF. Early legal review indicates uptime-crediting language can be implemented as a billing adjustment rather than amended SLA for the pilot, reducing legal complexity.
